name: the plain-global art fallback reads the <ul> again
why: Reverts testRowMatch()'s fallback to cell.querySelector(':scope > ul.mb-caa-art-ul').dataset.mbArtSearch. runFilter() matches SOURCE rows, which on a multi-table page carry the synced dataset attribute and never that <ul>, so a plain global query for an image type matches nothing. Must fail on 'H5: the plain global filter narrows to the one "Back" row' (1 expected, 0 rendered), while the regexp and column-filter controls stay green — they already went through getCleanColumnText().

name: the resolver drops the source row's synced attribute
why: Removes the mbArtSearchSync branch, leaving only the <ul>. This is the pre-existing channel _artSyncSearchTextToSourceRow() writes, so the CAA COLUMN filter — which reads the source row through getCleanColumnText() — loses its text too. Must fail on 'control: the column filter narrows its sub-table to the one "Back" row', which is what makes that control a guard and not decoration.

name: the resolver drops the rendered <ul> branch
why: Leaves only the synced attribute. On a multi-table page every source row has that attribute, so these tests cannot see the loss; it would show on a single-table page, where the <ul> is the only channel (allRows' rows ARE the rendered rows) and nothing syncs. KNOWN UNCOVERED: no committed single-table shell carries /cover-art anchors, which is the same gap AUDIT.md §3.1 H4b records.
